Kidnay, A.J., Parrish, W.R. and McCartney, D.G. (2019). Fundamentals of Natural Gas Processing, 3rd ed. CRC Press (Taylor & Francis Group), Boca Raton, FL. ISBN 978-1-138-61279-2. Copyright page dated 2020; no DOI printed.

Targeted pass over a 499-page textbook. Locators are PRINTED page numbers (PDF page = printed + 27). Main file: amine reboiler heat duty (kJ/L lean solution, NOT per m3 gas) and reboiler temperatures by amine (Table 10.3, from GPSA EDB 2016); TEG and molecular-sieve regeneration temperatures; capital costs from Example 19.1 (100 MMscfd plant, 2017 USD, Tannehill and Chandra 2018 curves) for DEA amine, TEG, cryogenic NGL recovery and liquid-redox sulfur, converted to per m3/yr or per t/yr with explicit formulas; compression $/hp (Sect. 19.1, Example 19.1, Sect. 17.2 stations) converted to $/kW; gas-turbine drive efficiency 28-35% LHV; San Juan plant electricity 8.8 MW for 13e6 Nm3/d (electricity only); modular gas-plant construction time 18 months; LNG energy 10-15% (base-load) and 1-3% (peak-shaving) of feed gas; LNG capex $400-1000 per t/yr (printed as $/Mtpa, a unit slip); levelized liquefaction costs (2003 and 2001); regasification energy and costs. Not loaded: Chapter 19 cost curves (Figures 19.1-19.6, log charts; not read), Table 18.5 netbacks and Table 18.7 shipping rates (market prices), pipeline costs per mile, property tables, worked exercises with assumed data. The book prints NO specific power (kWh/t LNG) by liquefaction process, no glycol reboiler duty, no NRU/helium energy and no Claus energy or cost numbers. Example 19.1 compression $1,400/hp conflicts with the $2,000-3,000/hp rule on p.429. Example 19.1 TEG cost ($6.3 MM) exceeds the amine cost ($5.0 MM) as printed.
